rows.name: Mele Market at Pearl at Kalauao
rows.schedule_text: Pearl at Kalauao's homepage lists its monthly night market for Wednesday, December 9, 5pm–9pm, billed as the end-of-2026 market. The regular schedule on the night-markets page is the last Wednesday of each month, 5pm–9pm. Dec 9 is not the last Wednesday, so the December date differs from the usual pattern.
rows.admission: Free admission (parking also free per earlier 2026 listings)
rows.description: Monthly evening night market at the golf-course venue with 100+ local vendors, live entertainment, food, desserts and shopping, per the organizer's homepage.
rows.notes: Kind corrected from holiday_fair to night_market. The name 'Mele Market' appears only on the third-party calendar. No Pearl page uses it. This is almost certainly the December edition of the Last Wednesdays Night Market, so treat it as a duplicate and merge. The 2025 December edition was branded 'Holiday Night Market' (KSBE alumni calendar, Dec 10, 2025). The organizer page does not list vendor types beyond food, desserts and shopping. The night-market Instagram named in Honolulu Magazine is @nightmarketcentral. Pearl's own events page points to @pearlatkalauao. source_date is null because the page is undated. Dec 9 is unusual for a 'last Wednesday' market, so recheck the date before publishing. Side 'central' follows a third-party grouping of this market under Central Oʻahu and Pearl Harbor; ʻAiea could also be read as leeward_ewa.

rows.name: Mililani High School Holiday Food & Craft Fair
rows.schedule_text: Saturday, November 21, 2026, 9:00am–2:00pm. The organizer holds two Food & Craft Fairs each school year, in November and April.
rows.description: Holiday food and craft fair benefiting MHS athletics. The organizer says it offers 220+ spots for food trucks, food pop-ups, crafters, artisans, retailers, and community and school groups.
rows.source_label: Organizer's own website (vendor update blog) and organizer vendor page
rows.notes: Organizer pages confirm the date and hours. The street address comes from a vendor's event listing (Donnie Ann Creations) for the April fair. Its organizer is MHSAF, a separate event from the Mililani Town Association's craft fairs (the MTA autumn fair is Sept 12 at Mililani Mauka Rec 5), so it is not a duplicate unless your skip list says otherwise. The Facebook and Instagram handle is as posted on the organizer's blog; the Facebook page itself was not opened. Admission is not stated for the November fair. The April shoppers page says parking is free. The vendor URL is the organizer's vendor-information page, not a confirmed application form. A third-party site (vendorsmap.com) repeats the Nov 21 9am–2pm listing.

rows.name: Mohala Farms CSA
rows.address: P.O. Box 204, Waialua, HI 96791 (mailing address only)
rows.schedule_text: CSA: weekly bundles. Slow Food Oahu (undated, roughly 2024) reports Thursday baskets with pickup at the farm or in Moʻiliʻili, an annual fee of $25 and three-month subscriptions. The farm's own sign-up page lists Full ($25) and Half ($15) bundles and says new members depend on available supply. Separately, the farm sells every Saturday, 8:30am–12pm, at the Waialua Farmer's Co-op Market behind the Old Waialua Sugar Mill.
rows.description: Nonprofit organic farm in Waialua selling produce through a CSA program and a Saturday farmers' market stall.
rows.source_label: Organizer's own website (©2026 footer); CSA terms from Slow Food Oahu
rows.notes: The farm's own current site confirms the CSA program, the Saturday Waialua market with times, and the phone 808-478-8469. It does not give a Thursday pickup day or the Moʻiliʻili pickup. Those details are still only from Slow Food Oahu (undated), and the CSA prices conflict between Slow Food and the sign-up page, so confirm with the farm before publishing. The Instagram profile @mohalafarms describes 'an organic farm located in Waialua, HI'. Its bio carries older market hours (Haleʻiwa market Thursdays, farm Saturdays 9–5) that contradict the website, so it may be stale. The Roots Program Kalihi Valley hub-partner list gives a different handle, mohala_farms, which I could not match to a live profile. The farm's own sign-up page shows the contact email mohalafarms@gmail.com. The contact page shows info@mohalafarms.org. The street address of the farm was not found in a first-party source; Manta shows 66-1380 Kaukonahua Rd but it is an unclaimed directory listing and was not used. Kind is left null because CSA is not in the allowed kinds. The farm's market stall is a vendor stall at the Waialua market, not its own market. The Facebook handle was not confirmed.

rows.name: OK Poultry (farm egg sales)
rows.schedule_text: Wednesday and Saturday only, per a food blog about two years old. A farm-directory listing gives 7:30am to 1pm on those days. The blog says to arrive before about 8:30am because eggs sell out. Hours are not confirmed from a current first-party source.
rows.description: Egg farm selling fresh eggs directly at the farm. It also sells under the Waimana TKG Eggs brand, which is stocked at some Oʻahu retailers.
rows.source_label: Onolicious Hawaiʻi blog posts (third-party); localmeatmilkeggs.org directory for hours
rows.notes: The address and Wed/Sat hours were filled from non-Yelp sources: the Onolicious post (address, phone 808-259-7832, and Instagram instagram.com/okpoultry), the localmeatmilkeggs.org directory, and a Hawaiian Local directory listing. Yelp was not used. A Honolulu Magazine feature (older) confirms the KK Poultry to OK Poultry ownership change and that eggs are sold at the farm. The older Onolicious post mentions a $15 tray of 30 medium white eggs; this is old pricing and not a current price. A Hawaiian Local directory lists okpoultry.com, and Nextdoor lists the business as K K Poultry Farm Inc (same phone). I could not open the website, so the website field is left null. No current first-party page or dated 2026 post was found, so current status is unconfirmed. Waimānalo is windward and borderline for the Honolulu/East scope.

rows.name: Red Barn Farmstand
rows.schedule_text: A Hawaii Life guide lists Wednesday through Sunday, 8:00am to 3:00pm, but this is likely outdated and the stand appears to be closed.
rows.organizer: Holoholo General Store / Twin Bridge Farms partnership (original operators)
rows.description: Opened in 2016 as an outdoor farmstand and café at Kamehameha Hwy and Cane Haul Rd in Haleiwa, selling local produce and prepared food.
rows.source_label: Hawaii Mom Blog (community article); Hawaii Life guide for the old hours
rows.notes: A December 2018 Hawaii Mom Blog post says Farm to Barn Cafe opened at the site of the former Red Barn Farmstand, which suggests Red Barn ended years ago. Aggregator listings (MapQuest, Wanderlog) also mark it permanently closed. The Hawaii Life guide's Wed–Sun 8am–3pm hours match older 2017 coverage and may be copied forward. I could not open redbarnfarmstand.com. The address 66-320 Kamehameha Hwy is also the address on Thrive Hawaii Family Farm's own site and Facebook page, so Thrive may now use or share that location; I did not confirm this. Phone per the Hawaii Life guide: (808) 753-4350. Recommend excluding unless a first-party source shows it is open.

rows.name: Taste of Korea in Honolulu
rows.schedule_text: One-day event held Saturday, May 16, 2026, 10am–3pm. The organizer's 2025 edition was Saturday, November 8, 2025 at Palama Settlement. No later edition has been found, so a repeat is unconfirmed.
rows.description: Free-to-attend-style Korean cultural festival with K-food, hanbok, crafts and traditional games for families, per the organizer's Eventbrite page.
rows.notes: The organizer's own Eventbrite listing shows the event has ended. It lists free parking on campus. The page does not state an admission price. The organizer's 2025 listing described the festival as free and family-friendly, but that does not confirm the 2026 price, so admission is left null. The street address is not stated in the sources, so I left it null. The 'side' is town because the listing says Honolulu; the neighborhood was not stated. A separate event with a similar name, also called Taste of Korea, is run by the Hawaiʻi Korean Cultural Center at Honolulu Country Club. Its 10th annual edition is on Nov 20 and tickets are $100 per KHON, so it is a different event and organizer. Do not merge them. An organizer website was not found. The event is over and the date has passed. Keep only if you want the one-time listing or a later edition is found.

rows.name: The East Honolulu Food Festival
rows.venue_name: Mary, Star of the Sea Church and Schools
rows.schedule_text: Annual, held on a Saturday in early May, 5:30pm–9:30pm. The 18th annual edition was Saturday, May 2, 2026. The 2027 date is not confirmed; a third-party calendar lists May 2027 as TBC.
rows.organizer: Mary, Star of the Sea Church and Schools
rows.admission: Ticketed, all-inclusive tasting ticket. The 2026 price is not stated in the sources I opened.
rows.description: Annual food festival with unlimited tastings from 20+ restaurants and purveyors, a silent auction, keiki activities and live DJ entertainment. The 2026 theme was 'Under the Moon in Old Hawaiʻi'. Free parking and shuttle from Kalani High School.
rows.source_label: Hawaii News Now (news), cross-checked with Aloha State Daily and Hawaii Mom Blog
rows.notes: The organizer, venue and 2026 date are now confirmed by several news and community articles from April 2026. I did not find an organizer website or social page, so confidence stays at medium. The Waikiki Beach Stays calendar still lists it under May 2027 with no date. The 2024 edition (16th) was ticketed at $95 for adults and $35 for keiki per KHON. I did not find the 2026 price. Chalk 2027 up as expected but unconfirmed.

rows.name: Thrive Family Farm / Thrive Ohana Farm CSA
rows.schedule_text: CSA runs in successive eight-week subscriptions (per Slow Food Oahu; undated). Organic produce was listed at $40/week. The farm's own events page lists 2025 CSA sign-ups and says to call 808-489-8305. A 2026 sign-up was not found.
rows.organizer: Thrive Hawaii Family Farm (Jennifer and Jason Witte)
rows.description: Small organic family farm in Haleiwa selling vegetables through a member-supported CSA and to North Shore restaurants.
rows.source_label: Organizer's own website and events page; Slow Food Oahu for the eight-week term
rows.notes: Website, handle and Facebook can now be tied to this farm. thriveohana.org names Jason and Jennifer Witte, shows the Haleiwa address, and its events page lists the same phone, 808-489-8305, as Slow Food. The Facebook page for Thrive Hawaii Family Farm shows the same address and phone, and a Merry Christmas 2025 post. The Instagram profile @thrive.hawaii is titled Thrive Hawaii Family Farm, and the Roots Kalihi Valley hub-partner list gives the same handle. I did not see the site's own link text, so the handle rests on the profile name plus the Roots listing. Roots gives thriveohana.com for 'Thrive Ohana Farm', which looks like the same business, but I used thriveohana.org because Slow Food and the farm's own pages use it. The website pages are undated (about 2024–25), and I found no 2026 CSA sign-up, so whether the CSA is currently taking members is unconfirmed. The CSA pickup location is not stated. The address is the farm's listed address, not a confirmed pickup point. The same address is also listed for the former Red Barn Farmstand. Kind is left null because CSA is not in the allowed kinds. Eight-week terms and the $40/week price come from Slow Food only.

rows.name: Waiahole Farm
rows.description: Windward-side fruit stand described in a recent TikTok roundup as selling fresh-cut fruit, juices and seasonal tropical fruit.
rows.source_label: TikTok discover page (third-party social mention, last updated 2026-10-26)
rows.notes: Still only a single social mention, which describes it as being on the windward side rather than the North Shore. The TikTok result is a recent social mention, but it does not give an address, hours, or official handle. Address candidates appear only on Yelp and MapQuest, which I did not use. A separate travel blog describes a Waiahole Farm with taro fields, and I could not confirm it is the same business as the fruit stand. No first-party page was found. Needs a first-party source before it goes in the directory. Waiāhole is windward, so side was corrected from the North Shore link in the URL.

rows.name: Waihuena Farm CSA
rows.address: 59-414 Kamehameha Hwy, Haleiwa, HI 96712 (across from Pipeline)
rows.schedule_text: The farm's homepage lists a roadside farmstand on Tuesdays, 12–6. Its 'Our Farmily' page says the Tuesday 12–6 farmstand and classes, and Wednesday 9–12 garden volunteer day, are by appointment only. A LocalHarvest listing (updated Jan 2025) says CSA members pick up shares at the farm fridge on Mon and Tue.
rows.description: Organically managed North Shore farm offering a CSA program and a herdshare. Products are offered through membership rather than direct sale.
rows.source_label: Organizer's own website (homepage and 'Our Farmily' page, undated)
rows.notes: The farm's own pages are now confirmed: waihuenafarm.com gives the address, phone (808) 551-8132 and email info@waihuenafarm.com. The homepage says the farm is not yet permitted for sales and offers products through a herdshare and CSA membership, so products are 'not for sale' in the usual sense. The homepage says the roadside farmstand is open Tuesdays 12–6. The 'Our Farmily' page says it is by appointment only. Confirm with the farm before listing it as a walk-up stand. LocalHarvest (third-party, updated Jan 21, 2025) lists a $25 weekly CSA share, 20 shares, and pickup at the farm fridge. The farm's own site does not state a price. Instagram and email shown in the Sierra Club list could not be recovered, so the handle stays null rather than guessed. The own pages are undated, so I could not confirm the current state.
